text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices is important for building reliable and easy-to-use services. First, choose clear and meaningful endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened, for example 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, provide good documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, such as /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. These simple rules help developers work with your API more efficiently and reduce confusion.
